answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a scarce, stake-backed signal: each account locks funds before it can endorse proposals, and endorsements count only in proportion to stake that remains slashable if later audits show coordinated fraud. A juniper reputation thread can link endorsements to prior audited work, so splitting funds across many fresh identities does not multiply voting weight. The attacker must acquire and lock real capital, then risks losing it; identities alone buy no influence.
